newsitem.title: USA: Stock fright sends US investors to T-bills-experts.
newsitem.headline: Stock fright sends US investors to T-bills-experts.

text.p: Fears that U.S. stocks may have peaked accounted for the flight-to-quality rush into the safe-haven U.S. Treasury bill sector, analysts said on Friday.
"There is no doubt this was a flight-to-quality move into the front end of the Treasury curve," said deputy chief economist Carol Stone at Nomura Securities International.
Stone was referring to the respective eight- and six-point drop in the yields of three- and six-month Treasury bills that coincided with a 247-point drop in the Dow Jones industrial average.

"It may be speculative buying of T-bills because they would become the most valuable instrument if the stock situation becomes more confusing next week," the trader said. "If any problems take place here, in Germany or elsewhere, short-term dollar assets is where people would want to be."
J.P. Morgan senior economist Marc Wanshel viewed the move into U.S. T-bills as "the typical knee-jerk reaction to a psychological perception the stock market is shaky."

"You buy bills not because there is a fear about liquidity, but on the thought that there may be a problem. It has its own dynamism," Wanshel said. "It's the typical flight to quality, nothing more than that."
